Omode:classicforge.title: Classic Forge-the-Crystal
Omode:classicforge.description: Bring the Adamant and Legend Sword to Kokkol to complete this objective. In this mode, you will not receive the Excalibur from Kokkol; instead the Excalibur replaces the Crystal in the pool of key items. This mode forces the Owin:crystal flag to be on.

Omode:classicgiant.title: Classic Giant%
Omode:classicgiant.description: Defeat the Giant of Bab-il to complete this objective. In this mode, there is no character reward for finishing the Giant.

Omode:fiends.title: Fiends%
Omode:fiends.description: Defeat Milon, Milon Z., Kainazzo, Valvalis, Rubicant, and Elements to complete this mode.

Omode:dkmatter.title: Dark Matter Hunt
Omode:dkmatter.description: 45 Dark Matters are randomly placed in chests (MIABs excluded); bring 30 of them to Kory in Agart to complete this objective.

Cj:spells.title: Characters learn J-spells
Cj:spells.description: White mages will learn Armor, Shell, and Dispel. All mages learn spells at the levels they would in FF4j.

Cj:abilities.title: Characters have J-commands
Cj:abilities.description: Characters retain the battle commands from FF4j that were removed in FF4us.

Cnekkie.title: Characters start with limited gear
Cnekkie.description: Characters start with a random low-level weapon and no armor. (Duplicate characters will have the same starting gear.)

Cnodupes.title: Duplicate characters not allowed
Cnodupes.description: If a duplicate character tries to join your party, instead nothing happens.

Cbye.title: Dismissed characters are irretrievable
Cbye.description: Dismissed characters cannot be retrieved. (Normally, dismissed characters go to the Mysidia crystal room and the Tower of Wishes where they may be reclaimed.)

Cpermajoin.title: Characters can't be dismissed
Cpermajoin.description: You have the choice of whether to accept each new party member, but once your party is full, you cannot recruit anyone else.

Cpermadeath.title: Permadeath
Cpermadeath.description: Party members that are "swoon" at the end of any battle are permanently removed from the game. (Does not apply to cutscene/story battles you are allowed to lose, ie. Dark Elf first round or Titan fight at Mist.)

Cpermadeader.title: Permadeader
Cpermadeader.description: Party members that are swoon or stone at the end of any battle are permanently removed from the game. (This includes the cutscene/story battles that you are normally allowed to lose; now you will game over if your party wipes during these battles.)

Chero.title: Hero challenge
Chero.description:
• The starting character is your hero.
• The hero is the only instance of that character available (unless other flags force it).
• The hero cannot be dismissed.
• The hero fights the Mt. Ordeals mirror room boss alone.
• Kokkol will craft an FF4 Advance weapon usable by the hero.
• The hero gains EXP even if incapacitated.
• The hero is your agility anchor.
• The hero is exempt from permadeath.

Tshuffle.description: Treasure contents are the same as in original FF4, but their positions are shuffled. This randomization is weighted so that overworld treasures tend to remain in the overworld, and similarly for underworld/moon treasures.

Tstandard.title: Standard chest randomization
Tstandard.description: A basic randomization, allowing items of reasonable strength to appear. Items are equally likely to appear in any chest regardless of location.

Tpro.title: Pro chest randomization
Tpro.description: A skill-testing randomization, limiting the strength of available items, and weighted to favor stronger items in later-game and infrequently-visited areas.

Twild.title: Wild chest randomization
Twild.description: An unrestricted randomization, allowing equal chance for items to appear in any chest, including the most powerful items.

Twildish.title: Wild-ish chest randomization
Twildish.description: Allows items of any strength to appear, including the most powerful items, but uses location-based weighting like the pro randomization.

Tjunk.title: Keep junk
Tjunk.description: Normally, poor-quality items in chests are replaced with an equivalent amount of GP (based on sell price) to reduce inventory bloat. Enable this flag if you want to keep them as items.

Tmoney.title: Everything is junk
Tmoney.description: Instead of their assigned contents, all chests contain an equivalent amount of GP, based on sell price (monster-in-a-box chests excluded).

Sshuffle.title: Shuffle shops
Sshuffle.description: The same items are available for sale in shops as in original FF4, but their locations are shuffled. This randomization is weighted so that overworld shop items tend to remain on the overworld, and similarly for underworld/moon shops.

Sstandard.title: Standard shop randomization
Sstandard.description: A basic randomization, allowing items of moderate strength to appear in shops, and weighted to place stronger items in later-game shops.

Sunsafe.title: No safety checks
Sunsafe.description: Normally, the randomizer guarantees Cure2 potions, Life potions and StarVeils are readily available, and that Cure3 potions are available in seeds without white mages. This flag removes those checks.

Spro.title: Pro shop randomization
Spro.description: A skill-testing randomization, limiting the strength of available items, and weighted to place stronger items in shops gated behind key items.

Swild.title: Wild shop randomization
Swild.description: An unrestricted randomization, allowing equal chance for items to appear in any shop, including the most powerful items.

Bstandard.title: Randomize bosses
Bstandard.description: The positions of bosses are shuffled. Boss stats are roughly scaled to match the battle it's replacing. For example, Rubicant in the Watery Pass would have the HP and speed of Octomamm. (Yes, this flag is janky, and a MegaNuke is still a MegaNuke. Save often.)

Bunsafe.title: No safety checks
Bunsafe.description: Normally, you are guaranteed a path to the underworld that does not require defeating the most difficult bosses. This flag removes that check.

Bnofree.title: No free bosses
Bnofree.description: All boss battle enemies have the "boss bit" set. The alternate win conditions are removed from the D.Knight, Karate, K/Q.Eblan, and WaterHag fights.

Balt:gauntlet.title: Alt Gauntlet
Balt:gauntlet.description: Replaces the Fabul Gauntlet boss with five unscaled normal enemy encounters from the nearby area.

Bwhichburn.title: Replace Wyvern's opening MegaNuke with random attack
Bwhichburn.description: The replacement attack will be weaker than MegaNuke (unless Bunsafe is enabled, in which case it may not be).

Etoggle.title: Random encounters can be toggled
Etoggle.description: Encounters can be enabled/disabled from the in-game Custom menu.

Ekeep:doors.title: Preserve TrapDoor fights
Ekeep:doors.description: Prevents the above encounter rate setting from applying to the TrapDoor fights in the Sealed Cave.
Ekeep:doors.group: Random encounter rate › Random encounters can be toggled

Ekeep:behemoths.title: Preserve forced Behemoth fights
Ekeep:behemoths.description: Prevents the above encounter rate setting from applying to the forced Behemoth fights in Cave Bahamut.
Ekeep:behemoths.group: Random encounter rate › Random encounters can be toggled

Edanger.title: Keep dangerous encounters
Edanger.description: Back attacks and "Surprised!" encounters will still occur, even when encounters are disabled via Etoggle or Enoencounters.
Edanger.group: Random encounter rate › Random encounters can be toggled

Enoexp.title: No EXP for random encounters
Enoexp.description: Bosses and monster-in-a-box fights still award EXP.

Gsylph.title: Allow Sylph MP glitch
Gsylph.description: When enabled, casting Sylph will only deduct MP from the caster if they are in the middle party slot.

-kit3:mysidia.title: Mysidia kit

-kit3:baron.title: Baron kit
-kit3:baron.description: 10 Headbands, 10 Karate gis, a Thunder Claw, and a Thunder Rod.

-kit3:dwarf.title: Dwarf kit

-kit3:eblan.title: Eblan kit

-kit3:green.title: Green Names kit
-kit3:green.description: A grab bag of items selected individually by FE devs without any coordination whatsoever.

-kit3:random.title: Select a random kit
-kit3:random.description: One of the other kit options, selected at random.

-noadamants.title: No Adamant Armors
-noadamants.description: Adamant Armors are not available. Trading the Pink Tail in the Adamant Grotto instead grants a strong item.

-smith:alt.title: Kokkol crafts a random tier 7/8 item

-smith:super.title: Kokkol crafts a weapon from FF4 Advance
-smith:super.description: Instead of the Excalibur, Kokkol the Smith will forge a weapon from Final Fantasy 4 Advance. (Some weapons have been modified slightly due to technical limitations.)

-exp:split.title: Split EXP distribution
-exp:split.description: Normally in Free Enterprise, earned EXP is not divided among the party, and each member receives the full amount. Set this flag to restore the original FF4 EXP distribution scheme (ie. earned EXP is divided among the surviving party members).

-exp:noboost.title: No low-level EXP boost
-exp:noboost.description: Normally in Free Enterprise, in a full party, low-level party members (at least 5 levels below the median level) earn double EXP. Set this flag to remove this bonus.

-exp:nokeybonus.title: No EXP bonus after 10 key items
-exp:nokeybonus.description: By default in Free Enterprise, once 10 key items have been collected, earned EXP is doubled. Set this flag to remove this bonus.

-vanilla:fusoya.title: Vanilla FuSoYa
-vanilla:fusoya.description: By default, Free Enterprise runs with the "FuSoYa Challenge", where FuSoYa begins with 500 HP and a collection of low-level spells, and each boss defeated grants him 100 HP and three random additional spells. This flag disables that challenge and restores vanilla's FuSoYa behavior, where he joins with 1900 HP and his full spellset.

-vanilla:agility.title: Vanilla agility anchoring
-vanilla:agility.description: FF4 scales the speed of combat based on the agility stat of your party's "agility anchor". In Free Enterprise, the anchor is always the first occupied party slot (in the sequence of middle, top, bottom, top-middle, bottom-middle). However, in vanilla FF4, if Cecil is in the party, then he is the agility anchor, regardless of position. Enabling this flag will restore that behavior, making the first Cecil in your party the anchor, if present. (Note that this overrides the Chero agility effect, if playing with the hero challenge.)

-vanilla:hobs.title: Vanilla Hobs spell
-vanilla:hobs.description: By default, instead of learning Fire1 at Mt. Hobs, Rydia will learn a random summon (other than Leviatan and Bahamut). This flag removes that behavior.

-vanilla:growup.title: Vanilla Dwarf Castle summons
-vanilla:growup.description: By default in Free Enterprise, the summons learned when Rydia ages are randomized. Set this flag to return to the vanilla summons learned at that time (Mist, Indra, Jinn, Shiva, and Titan).

-vanilla:fashion.title: Vanilla fashion
-vanilla:fashion.description: To help distinguish duplicate characters, Free Enterprise randomizes the battle palettes of each character. Enabling this flag preserves each character's original battle colors.

-vanilla:miabs.title: Vanilla monster-in-a-box locations
-vanilla:miabs.description: By default, monster-in-a-box chests are relocated randomly within the same dungeon/area. This flag forces MIABs to remain in their original positions.

-vanilla:giant.title: Vanilla Giant
-vanilla:giant.description: Removes the added exit at the start of the Giant of Bab-il, forcing you to complete it in order to return to the Big Whale. (Be careful not to get stuck with your only save file being inside the Giant.) This exit is restored once the Giant is completed.

-vanilla:z.title: Vanilla Z sprite
-vanilla:z.description: Free Enterprise replaces Zeromus' battle sprite with a random sprite. (Its battle behavior and stats are unchanged.) Enable this flag to preserve Zeromus' original battle sprite.

-vintage.title: Vintage Battlefield
-vintage.description: Enables the April Fools Day 2019 mode.

-pushbtojump.title: Push B to Jump
-pushbtojump.description:
• Enables the April Fools Day 2020 mode.
• This flag does not affect the randomized placement of progression items.
• Stability is absolutely not guaranteed.
• Instability is absolutely guaranteed.
• (If a door goes somewhere you don't expect it to go, it was probably a "return" door, which takes you back to your previous location.)
